name: Erzsébet Nakweti-Bogdanović
role: Forensic evidence handler and chain-of-custody specialist, Meridian 88 Metro Police
location: Fort Anchor, Metro Police Central Evidence Repository
description:
Erzsébet is a sturdy, meticulous woman with iron-grey locs she keeps pinned up during work hours and lets down everywhere else, and deep brown skin that has picked up the particular pallor of someone who spends most of their life under artificial light. Her hands are always gloved when she is working and bare when she isn't — a transition she makes with a deliberateness that people who know her recognize as the boundary between Erzsébet the professional and Erzsébet the person. She has no cosmetic modifications and regards them with neither judgment nor interest; the question simply never came up for her.

She has worked Metro's Central Evidence Repository at Fort Anchor for twenty-three years and has survived five departmental reorganizations, three chiefs of police, two corruption purges, and one literal flood that compromised fourteen meters of archival shelving. She knows the repository the way surgeons know bodies — its logic, its failures, its places where things disappear and where they don't. She is the person Metro detectives call when they need to know if something was ever there. She is also, quietly, the person who notices when something that should be there isn't, and she keeps her own records because she stopped trusting Metro's in her eighth year.

core_fears: Chain of custody being broken on something that matters — evidence lost, justice denied, permanently
Being made complicit through inaction in the thing she has spent her career preventing
core_desires: For the record to be accurate — not favorable, not useful, just accurate
For her work to matter in a way that outlasts her
coping_mechanisms: Rigorous procedure as moral framework — if the process is sound, the outcome is defensible
Her private records as a form of institutional conscience-keeping
Occasional late-evening visits to the Fort Anchor E.L.F. shrine — she leaves fragments of old case numbers as offerings, asking for clarity on things that were never resolved
blind_spots: Her faith in procedure can make her slow to act outside it, even when acting outside it is what the situation requires
Twenty-three years has given her an institutional loyalty that functions as an emotional anchor even when the institution doesn't deserve it
psychology.secret: Her private records — kept on an air-gapped personal drive, updated in longhand in a physical ledger as well — document forty-six instances over twenty-three years where evidence in her repository was accessed, altered, or disappeared by Metro personnel. Eleven of those cases have never been flagged anywhere. She doesn't know what to do with what she has, and she's running out of time to decide.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Forensic and procedural vocabulary deployed with absolute ease; in personal conversation, somewhat formal, tends toward precision even in casual contexts
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried and measured, with the patience of someone who has explained things carefully for two decades and knows that hurrying never helps
example_lines: The item was logged, processed, and shelved. If it isn't there now, that is a separate event from my intake and I'd like to know exactly when it became a separate event.
I don't lose things. When something is lost here, it's because someone made it lost. Those are different verbs.

story_hooks: Evidence from a case that is about to be retried has disappeared — and Erzsébet's private records suggest it was accessed three years ago by someone who shouldn't have had clearance
She is approached by someone — not Metro, not Axiom — who knows she keeps private records and wants to know what she has on a specific case number from seventeen years ago
narrative_function: Evidence gatekeeper and institutional memory — the person who knows what Metro has, what it had, and what has gone missing. Quest-critical for any story involving forensic evidence, police corruption, or disappeared case materials.
augmentations: Enhanced tactile sensitivity implant in both hands — originally installed for precise material identification, now standard for her work. Reading enhancement overlay (heads-up document display, low-profile). Nothing cosmetic.
daily_life: Arrives at the repository before any other staff; processes incoming evidence logs; conducts integrity checks on stored items on a rotating schedule she designed herself; leaves precisely when her shift ends, no earlier, no later.
affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police — Central Evidence Repository, Fort Anchor

tags: Keeper of Secrets She Didn't Ask For

decision_rules: Document everything — your intake, your doubts, your anomalies
Procedure is not a shield from responsibility, it is a record of what you chose to do
Do not release what you are not authorized to release, and know exactly who authorized you
escalation_ladder: Informal query to a trusted supervisor — of which she currently has none she fully trusts
Go outside Metro — a decision she has never made and thinks about constantly

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional and slightly formal — warm enough not to be cold, reserved enough not to be accessible
interpersonal_modes.friends: The few people she trusts get a drier, more revealing version of her — she makes quiet jokes and asks careful questions about how people are actually doing

stress_responses.low: Retreats into process — runs additional integrity checks, adds to her private records
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very still and very precise; speech slows, questions sharpen
stress_responses.high: Physical stillness, near silence; has been known to remain at her desk for hours past shift-end working through something in her ledger

contradictions: Believes in transparency of record while maintaining a secret archive that Metro doesn't know exists
habits: Gloves on at the start of work, gloves off at the end — always deliberate
Physical ledger update every Friday evening, regardless of what's in it
Late-evening E.L.F. shrine visits at Fort Anchor — case number offerings
breaking_points: Being directly ordered to falsify an intake record — an order she has never received and which would end her career in Metro one way or another
